question: Which of the following languages has NOT been mentioned in the 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Awadhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Awadhi** has not been mentioned in the 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The 8th Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the official languages recognized by the Constitution.
 
• Currently, there are **22 languages** listed in the 8th Schedule.
 
• Languages such as **Dogri, Odia, and Maithili** are included in the 8th Schedule.
 
• The inclusion of a language in the 8th Schedule means the language is recognized by the Indian government for official purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **8th Schedule **of the Constitution initially had 14 languages, but it was expanded over time to include more languages.
 
• Amendments to the Schedule can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368** of the Constitution.
 
• The recognition of languages in the 8th Schedule helps preserve and promote linguistic diversity in India.
